criteria.supported: All conditions and output dimensions fit, including count with its matching-detail list.
criteria.unsupported: A required operation, condition or output cannot be represented.

coverage.instructions: Can every condition and requested output fit this native contract? The primary operation is ONE of list/count/earliest/latest/sourceEvidence; per-record details and evidence limits are separate output dimensions, not additional aggregations. Count always also returns ALL matching records, including their requested performer/time/etc: counting and listing those same matches together is supported. A generic request to say which requested details are missing is supported through unresolvedDetails and does not require a separate personal-booking question. List/count may also request documented-status or personal-booking provenance facets for the same selected records. Pure sourceEvidence reviews those facets across all selected statuses (status=all). Earliest/latest with those extra facets, multiple different aggregations/groups, disjunctive filters, cross-record joins/change histories/actions, unsupported predicates or unrepresentable ranges remain unsupported. Source evidence never certifies actual non-cancellation, absent printed notices, ownership or complete personal calendars. Distinguish unsupported MEANING from missing PHOTO EVIDENCE: an expressible question remains supported even if record membership or requested details will be uncertain. Never simplify or drop a clause. This version also binds the requested document-versus-occurrence unit. Missing identity evidence is an evidence gap, not a reason to change the unit. Earliest/latest ordering, multiple result units in one answer, cross-unit joins and photo/seat/person counts are unsupported in this version.

unit.instructions: What entity must the answer list/count or discuss? Interpret the HUMAN question, not how many records/photos happen to exist. Documents are distinct tickets/booking confirmations; occurrences are represented concerts, shows or appointments. Three tickets can describe one concert. A request for photos, people, seats or another unsupported unit does not become documents. Choose unclear when this distinction cannot be settled. Never silently substitute a record count for an occurrence count.
